items.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017
items.q: Dixieland could encompass anything from the Dukes of Dixieland and Al Hirt and Pete Fountain, that sort of thing.

ctx.x: I’ve often had a hard time describing to someone, or to my own self, the difference, if there is any, between Dixieland and trad and Chicago and classic.

You know it’s so complicated. I mean here I’ve played it for 50 some years. But it’s pretty much the same. Now the trad people, and I do the quotes, I mean they want to dwell really early on back to the early days of the New Orleans jazz. And Dixieland could encompass anything from the Dukes of Dixieland and Al Hirt and Pete Fountain, that sort of thing. I mean they stuck to their guns as far as the literature is concerned, as far as the tunes, except Al Hirt, he kind of branched out to the pop thing with all his…
Didn’t your father play on steamboats?
